title: CLO International Academic Month Issue 4 (Part 1) Digital Fashion and Creative Design
description: The fourth issue of the CLO International Academic Month is here! This edition features a conversation with Cui Rongrong, Dean of the School of Fashion at Zhejiang Sci-Tech University, discussing the demands of modern lifestyles and the development of the fashion industry, as well as the prospects of digital intelligence brought by digital technology!
transcript:
In this video, I will share with you the results of our current digital technology, intelligent technology, and fashion innovation combined with the outcomes from fashion designers, scholars, experts, and researchers.  
I will mainly share from two aspects.  
The first is the demand for modern lifestyle and fashion industry development.  
The second is the demand for digital technology and fashion design innovation.  

The demand for modern lifestyle and fashion industry development is mainly based on three aspects.  
The first is the trend of modern cultural background and fashion style.  
The second is the new foundation of digital infrastructure and fashion innovation.  
The third is how digitalization can improve the efficiency of fashion design.  

Modern cultural background:  
The third is the demand for economic development to meet the needs of our future material culture, agriculture, and industrial information civilization.  
The third is the globalized vision under the background of big data.  
The fourth is the digitalization of intelligent information culture and fashion.  

The rapid development of digital technology provides a new development environment for fashion industry design.  
In fact, it also leads to the digitalization of our modern life.  
This is already very obvious.  
Everyone knows that we can't live without computers and mobile phones.  
Our shopping, consumption, entertainment, etc., are all centered around digitalization.  

In this context, we need to study the direction of our modern lifestyle.  
Beijing recently released a new lifestyle concept.  
There are all kinds of lifestyles.  
For example: home-cultivation, spiritual practice, traveling, doing strange things, retrograde, and so on.  
These are all some of the changes in our modern lifestyle under digitalization and informatization.  

I summarize it in four aspects.  
The most basic is to meet the needs of physical function to improve the level of ecological health.  
Why do we need to level up?  
To meet the basic needs of the physical body.  
But now we have entered an era of pursuing big health and ecological health.  

The second is to meet the needs of social function.  
There is a need to diversify society under the demands of social function.  
We are no longer satisfied with the basic needs of material and social life.  
We are no longer satisfied with the basic needs of social life and ecological health.  
We need to meet more social and safety needs.  
We need to meet the individualization of lifestyle that respects self-demanding functions.  
You can now see individualized customized services in the digital society.  
There are various individualized options available.  

The most important is to achieve the artistic preservation of self-value and mental needs.  
The revival of our current culture and the reformation of our culture.  

I will briefly talk about this.  
The transformation of lifestyle drives three changes in the fashion industry, such as digitalization.  
The main focus is on the transformation from emphasis on focus to distribution, from the group to personality, and from the market to the customer.  

Again, why do we need to make such a change?  
In our country's various policies, there is good strategic leadership.  
We have received national recognition in the digital technology system from the 14th Five-Year Plan and the original plan of 2035.  
The industrialization and digitalization of digital negative energy and intelligent design have become the current direction of development.  
Mainly, the Internet, artificial intelligence, big data, virtual reality, smart manufacturing, and industrial Internet provide strong conditions for the transformation of the fashion industry to manufacturing.  

In addition, digital technology has also been developed.  
In the fashion industry, the application of Claude is relatively popular in Europe and the United States, especially in some major fashion brands.  

How to better meet the fashion needs of the new lifestyle?  
How can digital and cultural innovation, content production, and security combine with various industries to cross-border Internet?  
The practical, real-life, and future intelligent design of fashion, digital industry development, and the development of fashion and technology design.  

We are now teaching at our fashion academy.  
There are many digitally rich people.  
So our school has also established a digital fashion design research center  
to build a digital fashion brand.  

The digitalization of fashion products mainly covers four aspects:  
Digitalization of resources  
Digitalization of production management  
Digitalization of operation management  
Digitalization of quality control  

Now cloud software has been able to penetrate the whole of fashion—from inspiration to investigation to final operation management.  
Digitalization of quality control in all aspects.  
Now we already have certain brands able to carry out digitalized design applications and management throughout the full process, even some Google tracking in the backend.  

In fact, the intelligentization of fashion design production mainly involves:  
Materials  
Human resources  
Financial supply  
Design of supply and production control  

In the process of design production, the foundation of the business is trend prediction.  
I particularly emphasize the design perspective: trend prediction.  
So technology supply, data information of business management, and customer information rely on many business management systems:  
ERP  
OAS system  
MES system  
AI trend prediction system  

These enable data fusion and high-resolution virtual imaging, constructing six intelligent big data platforms.  
Different from traditional design production and verification, now they are unified on one platform.  

In our Hangzhou, many small and medium-sized clothing companies have been using such processes extensively, especially in foreign trade.  
During this epidemic, the communication between these three countries and foreign trade companies has all been realized, providing convenience and efficiency for fashion design.  

The usual operation of our clothing brand process mainly involves research and development projects:  
From the collection of fabric pieces to the final production, from the collection of inspiration to learning design.  

Everyone knows the positioning of the crowd, whether young, middle-aged, or older.  
There are some fashion senses.  
How do we go from age, from this market, to fashion availability, and so on?  
Different perspectives for research and development.  

Traditional research used to rely on manpower, but now it often depends on data.  
The selection of products and details, as well as traditional research and development, even interviews, design drafts, designs of various patterns, fabric determination, and custom designs—whether coats, skirts, pants, tops, or bottoms—are all part of the process.  

The regular design process involves waste of time and work.  
The cost of communication is very high and the process is relatively long.  
From collection, review, repair, sample, review, repair, order meeting, we repeat it again and again.  
It is a cyclical process.  

Digital rich fashion design uses some AI design and AI popular trend prediction.  
It can follow certain rules and principles to quickly collect related pictures and documents from across the entire network, then combine business brand positioning and historical sales data.  

Then, on pattern design, you can also use digital methods to search for all theme materials based on keywords given by the designer—the more keywords, the more accurate.  
We can also use digital intelligence software to perform individual element creation and expand the composition of creative combinations.  
I will give you some examples later.  

The second process is communication and sampling.  
Fashion design intellectualization is mainly reflected in 3D design software, virtual reality test platforms, and other diversified data and information channels.  
Online design through 3D.  

Most designers today still use flat design software.  
3D design can simulate fabric almost 100% virtually—from texture to color, material to texture—all can be fulfilled in the sampling process with high-definition virtual mapping.  

We are still using platforms for modeling and plating, adjusting in trial.  
Many companies now do this on the platform, creating electronic samples and electronic crafts, including every seam line, its distance, and fabric—all achieved through virtual mapping methods.  
Customers can see and share this on the platform.  

The second part is the digital technology industry and fashion design innovation.  

First, the interaction between images, design, and production.  
The first is based on visual image production, especially applied in our creative design field.  
The entire process of our fashion industry involves innovation integrating digital technology with image innovation and some design innovation.  

How to integrate?  
Image is the most current element.  
By establishing a combination of machine vision and artificial intelligence, automatic integration of innovation and image design is realized.  

For example, now we can enter an image of a small shark swimming in a lake, a motorcycle model, a three-dimensional electric board, the combination of a lion and a turtle, etc.  
Then, in the artificial intelligence system, based on the language you input, it will create a new image.  

However, currently in the AI system and our chat system, how to ensure originality is a moral and ethical issue.  
In the creative process, original creation is very particular.  

Thus, there is an original database containing composition content.  
How do we create a basic database for original creation?  
A lot of innovation still needs to be through our usual original or normal accumulation of patterns and design elements.  

Second, based on three-dimensional software, pattern division and recreation are possible.  
You can use division art—a kind of production art and algorithmic art form using computers and mathematics to produce anti-reference symmetrical pattern design.  

In the creation of art rendering software like Mander and Sandy, these are all pattern division software.  
You can set formulas, adjust parameters, and create creative patterns of different art styles.  

I want to emphasize that through division art, the original creation remains paramount.  
Emphasize intellectual property.  
One cannot use other works for analysis without risk.  

Many artists, some of whom are relatively substandard, use software to create, which I do not consider art.  
But technology development is irreplaceable.  
Future technology will serve social life and production and can effectively help us create more artworks and art forms.  

Third is the automatic production of parameters guided by settings.  
Using online tools and programs such as Everypile, based on a pre-designed rich texture pattern library, designers can choose patterns to carry out multi-parameter adjustments.  
They can adjust size, density, and color of elements to generate unique personalized patterns.  

In short, the patterns predicted must have a cool presence.  
Many software programs have produced large databases, including some enterprises building their own databases to protect intellectual property.  

Fourth is digital pattern composition and design.  
The MiHui smart flower platform exists in the Jiangzhe area and contains many patterns.  
It combines flower-shaped sales malls, flower-shaped online smart design, and flower-shaped customized development into a comprehensive platform.  

Through artificial intelligence technology, it analyzes market collections and popular flower-shaped design programs, predicts trends, automatically creates patterns and compositions, and other creative designs.  
Of course, relative input and settings are required to generate rich patterns and colors.  

Automatic color analysis and color data information are achieved through multiple link development, digitalized, visualized, and managed by smart transmission systems.  
Using smart eyes and multi-lens image color measurement systems, small batches of products can be automatically colored and manufactured with smart formulas and color systems.  

We have a teacher on our team who specifically uses traditional clothing, applies different colors according to traditional clothing standards, and automatically colors them in application software to form rich classic color schemes.  
This work recently received recognition in a secondary SCI area.  

Third is the image color system.  
Based on the image color of petals, supplemental and superimposition functions, modeling the construction of the image, it automatically identifies scenes, analyzes them, and provides different color schemes.  

In this system, color matching is very rich and is based on automatic identification of different shapes.  

The third is texture.  

Fashion presents a new scene:  
First, the use of new materials.  
In original materials designed by fashion, not only the development of new materials is increased, but also technology-adjusted fashion products create a green technology ecosystem.  

Under the promotion of the theme of the original universe, ultra-high-precision 3D digital fabric simulation technology is used.  
As I mentioned earlier, on fabric and real data collection—many of our software already has a large fabric database.  

When designing, these high-precision fabric data in the library can be used anytime.  
Through AI physics engine implementation, this fabric can be virtualized.  
Previously, fabric patterns were purely created; now, they appear almost exactly like real materials.  

Second is the new scene of the original universe.  
The arrival of the virtual era makes digital fashion inevitable.  
We now have digital models and multicultural new scenes.  
Virtual technology and fashion must be perfectly integrated.  

I was thinking about our school's digital show this year on a wave bridge.  
This wave bridge is the surface of the water.  
Our wave bridge is a real show on the wave bridge, and the T-shaped extension data below the bridge is on our lake.  
We are working on the design plan.  
If successful, we will integrate the real show with the virtual show and change different scenes and spaces.  

After the epidemic, our graduation show will be very bright.  
Everyone is welcome to pay attention.  

Fourth is the sense of style.  
Style identification is important.  
Ultimately, our design still needs to show a style.  

The first is automatic replacement through smart software on the Internet, which is very convenient with various smart switches.  

The second is array design.  
Using store array focus objective analysis in virtual space to see where our eyes are looking and where our scene is.  

The third is style identification.  
The creative clothing style has a demonstration platform.  
By clothing and fabric style, detailed capture and analysis of style positioning clothing are realized, including emotional evaluation.  

Because for style identification, intelligence can effectively locate our design.  

Then our team, in terms of digitalization, has done the following:  

First, our team supports panoramic virtual interaction technology and digitalization of Chinese traditional silk.  
We start from the material of traditional silk, color decoration processes, and physical chemistry information, collecting traditional silk food and raw materials for digitalization processing and displaying Chinese silk characteristics in 3D.  
This provides an information library of traditional clothing art resources for fashion design.  

This digitalization involves triangular display and virtual imitation.  
Last year, we put this online and showed it for a while.  

Second is virtual imitation technology to achieve information technology and design innovation practice.  
We combine with Zhijiang University of Technology’s national-level fashion design virtual imitation experimental center.  
Silk culture is passed on to product design digitalization technology.  
The main laboratory of the cultural department uses the PC section and clothing brand retail terminal design online platform and other virtual interference platforms.  

In the knowledge of virtual experimental equipment and spare experimental materials, students perform traditional clothing observation in simulation scenes.  
Through digitalized digital design, students’ understanding of traditional clothing and fashion design is increased.  

On this platform, our students wear related virtual imitation teaching garments.  

At the same time, while doing social service, we are trying to do the following:  
We have a Bo Chuanxiguan that has collected a large number of traditional clothing items.  
We have taken these cultural items and carried out related drafting—drafting original patterns under the supervision of our team.  
This is self-developed traditional cultural items for stock collection, from which mass-produced drafts are made and imported into drawing software.  

Second creation is done digitally.  
As I said, building a database of basic patterns may take a long time through our own creation.  
The application of digital software helps extract drafts and mass-produce patterns, supporting second and third creation as well as division and structuring of patterns.  

With the support of software developed by ourselves, our basic pattern drafts have reached rapid growth in nearly a year.  
Now basically all curves have been drawn and can be closed and continuous but still need further optimization.  

This is what we extract from traditional clothing and use digital software to extract for deep mass-produced drafts.  
We are carrying out secondary creation combined with art, which guarantees intellectual property of our patterns.  

Then, this is digital pattern manipulation.  
We use Pattern Monster software to change shape, size, and color of patterns.  

Second, patterns generated by mathematical algorithms also create many strange or creative individual patterns.  

Third, through neural network software generating stylized images, we generate various AI images through language description.  
This changes and transitions styles, generating different patterns and images.  

Many software, as everyone knows, are drawing and painting software applied in our design.  

The most important thing we are now developing by ourselves are AI auxiliary design systems.  

Fourth is the MiHui software.  
MiHui software is relatively mature in shape creation.  
It allows free arrangement of single elements and background colors with various free switches.  
As long as basic patterns are rich, it can generate a large number of new patterns, including themed creations.  

This is what we do daily—at least through mathematical means, we can produce dozens of standardized, commercially viable pattern styles.  

The third aspect is diversification of numbers on Chinese media platforms promoting traditional vibrational memory and culture.  
This is based on AI and VR, predictable virtual verbal technology, and digital virtual reality to strengthen reality technology for live shows or language video connections, promoting traditional vibrational memory culture.  

We do traditional transmission and promotion with some stories behind ourilli.  

The fourth is virtual chip technology implementation.  
Information technology and design innovation:  
We are now using a three-dimensional human body measuring chair, clothing for male and female, plant style chair, three-dimensional virtual test platform, and some testing systems and equipment to carry out experiments on digitalization of clothing engineering, human body engineering, and comfort of new fabric design.  

Smart design provides practical environments and conditions because we have two such laboratories in our school.  
The relationship between clothing, human body engineering, and three-dimensional fabric is experimentally studied with relevant data.  
In the future, we will also use information-based methods to conduct experiments that are forward-looking and more technological.  

The fifth is smart visualization technology software to promote analysis of fashion development and trends.  
Everyone should be using this more widely now.  
We use smart software to analyze the current market and various markets to accurately predict future fashion development and trends.  

We can also use such mathematical analysis to broaden the scope of anti-fashion clothing, cultural human knowledge, and social issues, providing research methods for the development of future literature and new literature.  

Currently, analysis of fashion market trends in the United States is basically based on data analysis from smart software and case analysis.  
The University of Louisiana, where related research is conducted, uses this as a foundation.  

Finally, to summarize, the characteristics of digital fashion are:  
One, diversity of fashion.  
Digital fashion is defined as the intersection of the digital world involving various subjects, including biomechanical machinery imitation, design, computer, and information technology.  

Two, democratization of fashion personality.  
Wearable equipment is still in its early stages.  
I believe in our imitation fiber’s intelligent function identification, function protection, protection, and fabric perception, which will improve continuously.  
Increasingly, it can serve human ecological health and information transmission.  

Three, fashion ecology.  

Four, digital coalescence.  
Digital technology and artificial intelligence coalesce and coagulate, presenting a characteristic of integration within ourselves.  

These are the four characteristics of future digital fashion.  

I will briefly introduce our work related to digital intelligence.  
Please provide your comments and suggestions.  
Thank you.

**Application by SMEs**: Small and medium-sized enterprises, especially in Hangzhou, adopt these digital methods extensively, facilitating international trade and communication during crises like the COVID-19 pandemic. --- ## Digital Research and Development (R&D) Processes in Fashion This section explains the transition from traditional to data-driven R&D and the use of AI and digital tools in design, sampling, and production. - **Traditional vs. Digital R&D**: - Traditional methods relied heavily on manual labor, interviews, and physical samples. - Digital R&D uses data for product selection, pattern design, fabric determination, and customization. - **Challenges in Traditional Methods**: - Time-consuming and repetitive processes: collection, review, repair, sampling, and ordering cycles. - High communication costs and long lead times. - **AI-Enhanced Design and Trend Prediction**: - AI collects relevant images and documents from the internet using business brand positioning and historical sales data. - Digital tools allow searching for pattern materials via keywords, improving accuracy. - AI software supports individual element creation and composition expansion for innovative designs. - **Communication and Sampling Digitization**: - Use of 3D design software and virtual reality (VR) platforms for online design and sampling. - 3D virtual fabric simulation replicates texture, color, and material properties with high fidelity. - Electronic samples with detailed seam lines, fabric types, and measurements enable remote customer interaction. --- ## Digital Technology Industry and Fashion Design Innovation This section covers the integration of AI, machine vision, 3D software, and pattern generation technologies in creative fashion design. ### Image Interaction and AI-Driven Visual Design - **AI and Machine Vision**: Combine to automate image and design innovation. - **Example Inputs**: AI can generate novel images from textual descriptions, such as a shark swimming in a lake or hybrid creatures. - **Ethical Considerations**: Originality and intellectual property rights are critical in AI-generated content. - **Originality Databases**: Essential for protecting creative works and guiding AI-generated designs. ### 3D Software and Pattern Division Art - **Pattern Division Art**: Uses computational algorithms and mathematical formulas to create anti-reference symmetrical patterns. - **Software Examples**: Mander and Sandy enable parameter adjustments for unique artistic patterns. - **Emphasis on Intellectual Property**: Artists must respect original creations; unauthorized use risks infringement. - **Technology Role**: Supports social life and production, enhancing artistic output. ### Automatic Parameter-Based Pattern Production - **Tools**: Platforms like Everypile offer pattern libraries with multi-parameter customization (size, density, color). - **Database Creation**: Enterprises build proprietary databases to protect intellectual property. - **Pattern Quality**: Patterns are designed to have strong visual impact and commercial viability.
